pass_a_gloss: Not the witness in the open alone but also the one in the hidden let us contend to take up completely, so that we too may sound out like an apostle the saying: for this is our boasting, the witness of our conscience, that in holiness and purity of God we turned about in the world. And let us fasten to the apostolic saying the prophetic: and he knows the hidden things of the heart of us, and most of all if we are being led off on the road to death; when we will declare the thing said by witnesses alone to God: because on account of you we are being put to death the whole day, we were reckoned as sheep of butchery. And if ever from the mindset of the flesh a fear of the judges threatening us with death is slipped under us, then let us say to them the thing from the Proverbs: son, give honour to the lord and you will have strength, and apart from him do not be afraid of another.
pass_b_english: Let us strive to take up perfectly not only the martyrdom that is in the open but also the one that is in secret, so that we too may cry out with the apostle: “For this is our boast, the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and the sincerity of God we have conducted ourselves in the world” (2 Corinthians 1:12). And to the apostle's word let us join the prophet's: “But he knows the secrets of the heart” (Psalm 44:21), our heart, and above all if we are being led away to death. Then we will say to God the words that martyrs alone speak: “For your sake we are put to death all day long; we have been counted as sheep for slaughter” (Psalm 44:22). And if ever, out of the mind “of the flesh” (Romans 8:6), fear of the judges who threaten us with death steals into us, then let us say to them the word from Proverbs: “Son, honour the Lord and you will be strong, and besides him fear no other.”

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 21); the old English was a digest. The old English kept only the opening idea, tagged Psalm 44:22 as 2 Corinthians 1:12, moved the Proverbs line to section 20, and added an invented close ('Blessed then are the pure in conscience ...').
Mn read Μή; Todro γάρ ἐστε read τοῦτο γάρ ἐστι; νἀνεστράφημεν read ἀνεστράφημεν; oAnv read ὅλην; vie read υἱέ; μόνῶν read μόνων.
'Are being led away to death' (the road to death understood).
'Fear ... steals into us' (is put under, suggested to us).
